text:
**Short answer:** For most people, Nationwide FlexDirect is the better choice for the first year, mainly because of the switch bonus and interest. Monzo is better for day-to-day app use and for spending abroad. Many people use both, with Nationwide as the main account and Monzo for budgeting and travel.

**Nationwide (FlexDirect)**
- **Switch bonus:** Nationwide is offering £175 when you switch using the CASS. You need to pay in £1,000 and make one debit card payment within 31 days. You can get it once on a personal account and once on a joint account. No end date has been confirmed.
- **Interest:** 5% on in-credit balances up to £1,500 for the first 12 months for new members, then 1%.
- **Cashback:** New FlexDirect customers can now get up to £10 a month alongside the 5% interest. Older reviews quote lower cashback figures, so check Nationwide's site for current terms.
- **Overdraft:** There is a £50 interest-free buffer by default. Beyond that, the rate is a flat 39.9%.
- **Branches:** It has 605 branches, kept open until at least the start of 2030. That helps if you want to pay in cash or cheques or talk to someone in person.
- **Weak spot, abroad:** FlexAccount has a 2.99% non-sterling fee. One comparison also lists 2.99% on FlexDirect purchases and cash.
- **Weak spot, app:** The app has improved a lot but isn't as good as Monzo, Starling or Chase.

**Monzo**
- **App and budgeting:** This is its main strength. Pots, instant notifications and spending insights are widely rated above high-street apps.
- **Abroad:** It charges £0 on card spending, and EEA withdrawals are unlimited in the worked example. Cash withdrawals outside the free allowance can carry fees.
- **Overdraft:** The free account has no automatic buffer. You apply for an arranged overdraft at 19%, 29% or 39% EAR depending on your credit score.
- **Paid plans:** The free account is enough for most people, but paid plans cost up to £19 a month.
- **Cash:** Paying in cash goes through PayPoint or the Post Office at £1 per deposit.
- **Switch bonus:** None listed.

**How to choose**
- **Pick Nationwide** if you want the £175 bonus, occasionally use branches or cash, or might want a Nationwide mortgage or savings later. Moving your salary and Direct Debits across for the bonus also fits a "main account" role.
- **Pick Monzo** if you're mostly digital, travel often, or want strong budgeting tools.
- **Use both** if you want the bonus and the better app. Switch your main account to Nationwide with CASS, then keep a free Monzo account for spending and pots.

**Caveats:** The £175 only applies if you haven't had a Nationwide switch bonus on a sole account since 2021. The 5% rate drops to 1% after a year, and you can't switch from an existing Nationwide or Virgin Money account. Both are covered by the £120k FSCS protection (Nationwide's figure is £120k per person per firm), so safety shouldn't decide it.
